_comment: DOM-67 pacing targets. These are DESIGN TARGETS, not game constants — the game never reads this file. RATIFIED 2026-09-11 by Jake, with one amendment: level 120 in one year of committed play. The simulator scores the live tuning against them; docs/specs/09-economy-pacing-targets.md is the prose version.

breakEven._comment: DOM-79, ratified 2026-09-11 (Jake): fighting's break-even wallet sits at this many hours of best-job income at the player's level, evaluated at the nominal win probability. Win rewards (enemies.json, and the snapshot-reward formula when matchmaking lands) are sized to hit it; loot.defeatLossRate stays the fixed proportional drain. defeatLossCap stays null (uncapped) for v1 — revisit with DOM-78 telemetry.

cloutIncomeMix._comment: DOM-81, ratified 2026-09-11 (Jake): target share of a committed player's earned Clout per day, held at every checkpoint level. Grind-led — the late game stays reachable without fighting, just slower. Recruiting is recorded as FLAVOUR (crew.cloutPerRecruit stays a flat 250, not an income source); its 0.05 is headroom, so moves and fights are sized to carry the whole target at 60:35. tools/econ-sim/gen-catalog.js realizes this mix in data/jobs.json and data/enemies.json.

playerProfiles._comment: Share of daily pool regen actually spent. Committed ~= plays every session to empty pools; casual logs in twice and leaves regen on the table; grinder is the ceiling case for exploit math. Spender profiles are committed usage plus a weekly boost budget (usdPerWeek), spent daily on the best Clout-per-dollar SKU path — the headroom check that paid pacing relief cannot shortcut the curve.

assumptions._comment: Modelling assumptions where the game data is silent. Each one is a gap the sim surfaces; none is a decision.
assumptions.spotAccrualNote: Spots have no accrual rate in tuning.json — the prototype pays full income per tap, min 60s apart. The sim models the INTENDED design (collect on login, sessionsPerDay collects) and separately prints the prototype exploit ceiling (60 collects/hour).
